title: A Peek Inside the Pompeii of Greece
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryA Peek Inside the Pompeii of GreeceIt’s a treasure trove of Minoan art and antiquesDNBy David Nield1:00 PM CDT on August 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEven for a country with a past as rich and storied as Greece’s, the ancient city of Akrotiri stands out amongst its historical sites.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Diamonds for Rain? Other Planets May Experience This!ShareNextStayThe ruins of the Bronze Age metropolis sit on the volcanic island of Santorini, in the southern Aegean Sea, some 120 miles southeast of the mainland. Excavations began in earnest on the island in 1967, and on Aug. 19, 1969, the city was uncovered in its entirety—frozen in time, as Pompeii would be thousands of years later, by a thick coating of pumice and ash.That pumice and ash came from a giant eruption that archaeologists think happened sometime in the 16th century B.C.
